messages:
jade.customer: Hey team — our April invoice (INV-2025-04-822) shows ~380 dedicated GPU hours charged. The Redwood console for account acme-prod shows 300 reserved hours used. Who can explain the ~80-hour difference? We didn't intentionally use burst capacity.
maya: Thanks for flagging, @jade.customer. Can you paste the account id and the invoice line items? Also did you have any autoscale policies that allow burst? @billing-bot can start a billing lookup.
billing-bot: Started lookup for invoice INV-2025-04-822. Pulling account acme-prod bundles and invoice lines. This may take a few mins.
jade.customer: Account ID = acct_0a1b2c3d. Invoice lines: "Dedicated reserved commit: 4 GPUs x 720h = 2880 GPU-hrs (billed as 288h-equivalent?)" — billing format is confusing. There's also an "On-demand burst usage" line for 82.34 GPU-hrs.
maya: Copying the invoice lines is super helpful. Quick note: the console has a couple of different views — "Reserved usage" vs "Total dedicated + burst". I'll escalate to eng telemetry to verify meter records.
raj: Hi @maya / @jade.customer, I'm on telemetry. Initial lookup in infra logs shows several allocations to the burst pool during Apr 12-14. Snippet:

```
2025-04-12T02:14:08Z runtime_burst_allocate account=acct_0a1b2c3d pool=burst gpus=2 duration_h=12 reason="autoscale_peak"
2025-04-13T18:07:22Z runtime_burst_allocate account=acct_0a1b2c3d pool=burst gpus=4 duration_h=24 reason="autoscale_peak"
```

raj: Those events sum to ~80 GPU-hours; that matches the invoice's on-demand burst usage line. The important distinction: reserved commit is billed as a monthly capacity fee (for 4 GPUs reserved) regardless of usage, but burst events are additional on-demand GPU-hours billed separately.
jade.customer: We thought reserved commit covers short spikes — is burst expected when reserved capacity exists? We had 4 GPUs reserved, why did autoscale route to burst?
maya: Good Q. @raj — can you confirm whether reserved nodes were fully saturated or if a routing decision caused fallback to burst incorrectly?
raj: Digging deeper. Query we ran against telemetry (simplified):

```
SELECT sum(duration_h * gpus) as gpu_hours, pool
FROM telemetry.allocations
WHERE account_id='acct_0a1b2c3d' AND time >= '2025-04-01' AND time < '2025-05-01'
GROUP BY pool;
```

raj: Result:
- pool=reserved => 300 GPU-hrs
- pool=burst => 82.34 GPU-hrs

raj: The autoscaler hit a bug where during a brief control-plane/backpressure event it could not attach to two reserved racks (a known under-replicated signal). Policy fallback allowed burst allocation even though a small amount of reserved capacity was potentially reclaimable later. TL;DR: burst usage is real and billed; console "Reserved usage" view only shows reserved pool consumption by default, so initial look missed burst rows.
jade.customer: Ok that explains numbers. Two follow-ups: 1) can you confirm pricing (burst vs reserved) and whether we can get a credit for the burst hours caused by the autoscaler bug? 2) how can we prevent this from happening again?
maya: Pricing: reserved commit is flat monthly (you already paid that). Burst is billed at on-demand rate (you can see per-GPU-hour price on the invoice line). I'll open a billing adjustment request for a goodwill credit while eng fixes the autoscaler behavior. @billing-bot please open ticket against billing queue referencing INV-2025-04-822 and attach raj's telemetry findings.
billing-bot: Billing ticket #BILL-2025-132 opened. Linked invoice INV-2025-04-822. Attaching telemetry logs from eng-telemetry.
raj: For prevention, two things:
- Short term: we'll push a control-plane guard so autoscaler prefers reserved attachments while reserve reconciliation is in progress. Small PR ready, will deploy to canary tonight.
- Medium term: add a console alert for "burst > X% of reserved for > Yh" per-account so you get notified immediately.

raj: Quick repro steps for our internal playbook:
1) Create account with reserved commit (4 GPUs) and an autoscale policy that allows burst.
2) Simulate attach failures on reserved hosts (kill attach-controller) for ~5-20m.
3) Trigger load that requests more capacity than currently attached reserved nodes.
4) Observe runtime_burst_allocate events and verify billing meter emits pool=burst.
maya: Action plan for customer:
- We will request a one-time billing credit for the 82.34 GPU-hrs billed as burst due to autoscale fallback. (Billing will review & confirm.)
- Eng will push the canary fix tonight and confirm no further regressions for your account.
- We'll also enable a burst-usage alert on your console and share instructions to opt-out of burst in the autoscale policy if you prefer.
jade.customer: Thanks, appreciate the transparency. Please keep me posted on the billing credit and the canary deploy. If you need any more invoice artifacts from our side let me know.
maya: Will do. Marking this thread for follow-up once #BILL-2025-132 updates. :thumbsup:
eng-telemetry: FYI — PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/897 (guard: prefer-reserved-attach). Deploying to canary now.
maya: Closing loop here after billing confirms. Thanks everyone.
